reasons: The file has no behaviour, so its correctness depends on the files that use it.
The version bump is a manual step that the header relies on, and nothing enforces it.

terms.meaning: a named description of the shape that data must have, so mistakes are caught early.
a fixed value that does not change while the program runs.
the decision for one criterion: it discriminates, it does not discriminate, or the check refuses to decide.
a valid answer where the data cannot support a decision, given with a stated reason.
the two groups being compared, here projects that overran against projects that were delivered.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and the three rules
sections.what: Header comment that states the question the check answers and the three hard rules: unknown is never counted as not met, every threshold is a setting, and a refusal is a valid result.
sections.why: Sets the principles every other E14 file must follow.

sections.name: E14Params
sections.title: Engine name and version
sections.what: Gives the engine's name and its version number, which must change whenever verdict behaviour changes.
sections.why: Stops two different versions of the check from looking like the same measurement, as the comment explains.
sections.watch_out: The version is changed by hand, so forgetting to bump it silently mixes results.

sections.name: E14_PARAMS, OUTCOME_GROUPS, OutcomeGroup
sections.title: The settings that verdicts depend on
sections.what: Lists each setting the verdict uses, such as the significance level, power, minimum gap, equivalence band, minimum projects per group, the largest share of unknowns allowed, and the fact floors. Each one is documented in the code.
sections.why: Puts every threshold in one place and tags the set, so a changed setting is visible in the output.
sections.watch_out: Editing a default changes every run that uses it, and only the tag shows that the change happened.

sections.name: CONTRAST, CriterionState
sections.title: Groups and contrast values
sections.what: Lists the four outcome groups and defines the contrast between the Overran and Delivered groups. Cautionary and In progress are reported but not compared.
sections.why: Fixes which groups the verdict compares, so the choice is visible in one place.
sections.watch_out: The contrast is fixed here, so changing which groups are compared needs a version bump.

sections.name: DefinitionId, Verdict
sections.title: Definitions and verdict options
sections.what: Defines the two ways to decide a criterion appears in a project, presence and salience, and the three verdict options.
sections.why: Keeps the two readings side by side because each fails in a different way.
sections.watch_out: Presence can be inflated by large fact counts, while salience needs more facts per project.

sections.name: RefusalReason
sections.title: Reasons for a refusal
sections.what: Lists the five refusal reasons, such as too few projects in a group, too many unknowns, too little power, an interval that spans the decision line, and no variation.
sections.why: Lets a refusal explain itself rather than appear as a bare failure.

sections.name: CriterionRef
sections.title: Shape of one criterion
sections.what: Defines the shape of one criterion: its id, whether it is a pillar or a sub-driver, which pillar it belongs to, and its name.
sections.why: Lets sub-drivers link back to their pillar.

sections.name: ProjectObservation
sections.title: Shape of one project's observation
sections.what: Defines one project's outcome group, fact count and state for each criterion, where a missing criterion is treated as unknown.
sections.why: Holds the input that the validator counts.
sections.watch_out: A criterion left out of the states is read as unknown, so a bug that drops keys makes results look less complete rather than wrong.

sections.name: RubricInput
sections.title: Shape of the full input
sections.what: Defines the input to the validator: the industry, the definition, the settings, the criteria and the observations.
sections.why: Gives the validator one input bundle.

sections.name: GroupCounts
sections.title: Counts for one outcome group
sections.what: Defines the counts for one group: total, unknown, resolvable, met, not met and the rate, where the rate is null when nothing is resolvable.
sections.why: Keeps the rate from showing a false zero when there is no data.

sections.name: CriterionResult
sections.title: Result for one criterion
sections.what: Defines everything reported for one criterion: both group counts, the gap, the range, the effect size, the exact p-value, the sample size needed, whether it is underpowered, the verdict, the refusal reason and a plain sentence explaining it.
sections.why: Gives a reader every number behind a verdict in one place.
sections.watch_out: The p-value is reported next to the range but the verdict rests on the range, so readers should not treat the p-value as the decision.

sections.name: PillarRollup
sections.title: Roll-up for one pillar
sections.what: Defines the summary for a pillar: its own verdict and gap, and counts of its sub-drivers by verdict.
sections.why: Lets the report show pillars with a summary of their sub-drivers.

sections.name: E14Report
sections.title: The full report
sections.what: Defines the complete report: engine name and version, settings echoed back, group sizes, facts per group, criterion results, pillar roll-ups, totals and refusal counts.
sections.why: Makes the report self-describing, so it can be read without the code.
sections.watch_out: Group sizes come first in the report because they limit every verdict below them.

summary: Defines the shared shapes and fixed settings for the E14 check, so every E14 file uses the same words for criteria, verdicts and reports.
purpose: Acts as the agreed vocabulary for the whole E14 check, with no logic of its own.
why: The header says it holds only types and constants, so the validator, the stats helpers and the database-facing builder can share one vocabulary without importing each other.
how: 1. Sets the engine name and version. 2. Defines the default settings in one tagged set. 3. Lists the outcome groups and the contrast being tested. 4. Defines the two ways to read a criterion (presence and salience), the verdict options and the refusal reasons. 5. Defines the shapes for criteria, project observations, group counts, criterion results, pillar roll-ups and the full report.
inputs: None at run time. It only defines data shapes and fixed values.
outputs: Type definitions and constant values such as the default settings and the version number, used by the other E14 files.
risks: The version number must be changed by hand whenever verdict behaviour changes, and nothing checks that this happened. Changing the default settings changes every new run, so the tag must change too.
debug: If a report field seems missing, find its shape here. If a verdict differs from an earlier run, compare the settings tag and version number in the saved report. Check the default values in the settings object.
